outcome: identification of causative organisms (species and count)
cohort: The study included 33 women who underwent a hysterectomy for puerperal sepsis at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital in Johannesburg between January 2019 and December 2019.
finding: Hysterectomy for puerperal sepsis was most frequently associated with prior caesarean section and hypertensive-related disorders, with Acinetobacter baumannii being the most common isolated organism, and a mortality rate of 6% in the studied cohort.
mod_finding: Hysterectomy for puerperal sepsis was most frequently associated with caesarean section (88% of cases), with nearly half of these CS procedures performed for foetal distress.
